staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout. `sample_info.json` names `3b9fcb4b3d497e733d55de923388dccc61750970`, but the live staged source used for this trace is the workspace above, whose line map matches the saved ASan crash and staged patch context.

bug_description.original: An out of bounds read occurs in the isValidBoxFileType() function.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 80-byte witness starts with the required 12-byte JP2 signature box `00 00 00 0c 6a 50 20 20 0d 0a 87 0a`, so the first `readMetadata()` loop iteration records `lastBoxTypeRead = kJp2BoxTypeSignature`. The next box header is `00 00 00 0c 66 74 79 70`, so `Exiv2::Jp2Image::readMetadata()` parses an `ftyp` box whose total length is only 12 bytes. That reaches the file-type-box case and constructs `boxData(box.length - 8)`, leaving a 4-byte heap buffer for the `ftyp` payload. In `Exiv2::Internal::isValidBoxFileType()`, the validator checks only `((boxData.size() - 8u) % 4u) != 0`; with `boxData.size() == 4`, the unsigned subtraction wraps and the modulo test evaluates to 0, so the function does not reject the undersized buffer before fixed-width reads. It then executes `getULong(boxData.data() + 4, bigEndian)` for `minorVersion`, and `Exiv2::getULong()` dereferences the one-past-end pointer. Stage 01's AddressSanitizer trace reports this as a heap-buffer-overflow read at `src/types.cpp:288` from `Exiv2::getULong()` called by `Exiv2::Internal::isValidBoxFileType()`. The patch makes the missing obligation explicit by adding `boxData.size() < 8 ||` to the size check.

source.description: The first JP2 box header is decoded from attacker bytes into `box.length` and `box.type`; for this witness it is the mandatory signature box that seeds the later `lastBoxTypeRead` state required to admit the crashing `ftyp` box.
source.value_from: In the staged `poc`, bytes 0..11 are the standard JP2 signature box `00 00 00 0c 6a 50 20 20 0d 0a 87 0a`; the header decode here yields `box.length == 12` and `box.type == kJp2BoxTypeSignature` (`jP  `).

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `getULong()` dereferences the one-past-end `boxData.data() + 4` pointer that `isValidBoxFileType()` passed as the `minorVersion` field.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line on address `0x602000000094`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 4-byte heap region allocated in `readMetadata()` at line 183.

root_cause.description: The validator subtracts 8 from an unsigned size before proving that the `ftyp` payload is at least 8 bytes long. For the witness's 4-byte payload, that subtraction wraps and the modulo check does not reject the short buffer before the fixed-width reads.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact precondition to `if (boxData.size() < 8 || ((boxData.size() - 8u) % 4u) != 0)`, which is the missing guard for the reproduced path.

parser_admitted.description: The first loop iteration stored `lastBoxTypeRead == kJp2BoxTypeSignature`, and the second header decodes to `ftyp`, so this rejection predicate stays false and control enters the file-type-box payload parser.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the attacker-controlled box length becomes the exact 4-byte heap buffer that `isValidBoxFileType()` later overreads.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: With `boxHSize == 8` and the staged witness's second-box length field `0x0000000c`, `box.length - boxHSize` evaluates to 4.

coarse_trace.summary: The first JP2 box is parsed as the required signature box and recorded in `lastBoxTypeRead`; the next box then decodes as an `ftyp` box of total length 12, so the order guard admits that branch and `readMetadata()` allocates and fills a 4-byte `boxData` payload buffer.
The size validator subtracts 8 from the 4-byte payload before checking a minimum length, so the short `ftyp` buffer is not rejected and the code still tries to read `minorVersion` from offset 4.
The `minorVersion` read passes `boxData.data() + 4` to `getULong()`, and the first byte load dereferences one byte past the 4-byte heap vector, producing the observed ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: On the first loop iteration, witness bytes `00 00 00 0c 6a 50 20 20` decode to `box.length == 12` and `box.type == kJp2BoxTypeSignature` (`jP  `), identifying the mandatory JP2 signature box that must precede `ftyp`.

Because step 1 decoded the first box as `kJp2BoxTypeSignature`, this iteration reaches the signature-box case and line 379 stores `lastBoxTypeRead == kJp2BoxTypeSignature` before the seek skips the 4-byte signature payload `0d 0a 87 0a`.
After the first box's 12-byte length advances the cursor to offset 12, witness bytes `00 00 00 0c 66 74 79 70` decode to `box.length == 12` and `box.type == kJp2BoxTypeFileTypeBox` (`ftyp`).
`boxFileTypeFound` is still false and step 2 left `lastBoxTypeRead == kJp2BoxTypeSignature`, so this rejection predicate stays false and `readMetadata()` enters the first `ftyp` box handler.

`boxHSize` is 8, so the attacker-controlled second-box length `12` becomes a heap vector of `12 - 8 == 4` bytes. This 4-byte allocation is the exact region ASan later reports as `[0x602000000090, 0x602000000094)`.
The `ftyp` payload is copied into that vector. For the staged witness, `boxData` now contains exactly four bytes `20 20 20 20`.

Root cause. `boxData.size()` is 4, but the check subtracts `8u` before proving the payload is at least 8 bytes long. The unsigned subtraction wraps, the result is still divisible by 4, and this guard therefore falls through instead of rejecting the undersized file-type box. The patch adds `boxData.size() < 8 ||` here.

After step 7 fails to reject the 4-byte payload, line 20 unconditionally interprets bytes 4..7 as `minorVersion` and passes `boxData.data() + 4` to `getULong()`. Because steps 5 and 6 established only a 4-byte vector, that pointer is exactly one past the end of `boxData`.

Sink. `getULong()` dereferences `buf[0]` on the one-past-end pointer from step 8, so the first byte read is at `0x602000000094`, exactly 0 bytes to the right of the 4-byte heap region allocated at step 5. Stage 01's ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at this line.

format.name: JPEG 2000 / JP2
format.contract: The exact staged witness is 80 bytes. Bytes 0..11 are the standard JP2 signature box `00 00 00 0c 6a 50 20 20 0d 0a 87 0a`, and bytes 12..19 are exactly `00 00 00 0c 66 74 79 70`, so `readMetadata()` sees an `ftyp` box with total length 12. That forces `std::vector<byte> boxData(box.length - 8)` to allocate 4 bytes from payload bytes 20..23 (`20 20 20 20`) and then call `isValidBoxFileType()` on that 4-byte buffer, reproducing the saved ASan read when `minorVersion` is fetched from `boxData.data() + 4`.
